analysis_findings.description: 10.0.4.40 probed 120 ports on 192.168.10.10 in 5.9 s; 120 of 120 attempts (100%) were rejected or unanswered. This pattern matches network reconnaissance or an inventory scanner; check if it is authorised.
analysis_findings.title: Port scan (vertical)

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.3.30 queried 30 names under example.net, 30 of them with long or high-entropy first labels (e.g. ysqpo53r5l3oen3kmhqf52t3d72csnebey5yswwv5t2ap.t.example.net); 30 TXT queries, NXDOMAIN ratio 67%. Encoded data in DNS names is used by tunneling and some exfiltration tools, but also by CDNs and anti-virus lookups.
analysis_findings.title: Tunneling-like DNS names under example.net

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.4.40 probed port 445 on 25 hosts in 4.8 s; 25 of 25 attempts (100%) were rejected or unanswered. This pattern matches network reconnaissance or an inventory scanner; check if it is authorised.
analysis_findings.title: Port scan (horizontal)

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.2.20 connected to 203.0.113.50:8080/tcp 12 times every 60.1 s (±0.7 s, interval CV 0.012) with similar sizes (size CV 0.000). Regular timing is typical of automated check-ins (updaters, agents, C2); confirm the client.
analysis_findings.title: Periodic connections (beacon-like)

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.5.50 received application/x-dosexec content from 203.0.113.70 (/dl/payload.exe) without TLS: the file could have been tampered with in transit and its origin is unauthenticated.
analysis_findings.title: Executable downloaded over cleartext HTTP

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.1.12 and legacy.example.org (203.0.113.32) negotiated TLSv10, which is deprecated (RFC 8996) and lacks modern protections.
analysis_findings.title: Legacy protocol version TLSv10
TLS certificate outside its validity period

analysis_findings.description: selfsigned.example.org (203.0.113.30) presented a self-signed certificate (CN=selfsigned.example.org). Normal for test and internal services; on the internet it defeats server authentication.
analysis_findings.title: TLS server presented a self-signed certificate

analysis_findings.description: 10.0.5.50 sent HTTP requests with Host '203.0.113.70' (no domain name), e.g. GET /dl/payload.exe. Common for malware staging and scanners, also for appliances and internal tools.
analysis_findings.title: HTTP request to a bare IP address
